Yes, absolutely — once I've saved something, that saved information is mine and I don't want it quietly changed out from under me. If a page later rewrites its title or description, or even goes away entirely, Link Home should hold on to what I've got: the title and description as they were when I saved (or as I edited them), and definitely my labels and my note. Those last two especially — I chose those labels and I wrote that note in my own words, so nothing on the outside web should ever touch them.

The thing I'd hate is opening my collection one day and finding a bookmark's description has silently become something different because the site changed, or worse, my note vanished because the page went down. That would make the whole collection feel untrustworthy. The whole point of saving a link is that I've captured it — my copy shouldn't drift just because the original did.

So: keep everything I've saved, and never silently replace my information. If anything, if the page does change and you can tell, I'd rather you just let me know and let me decide whether to update it — but the default must be "leave my saved details alone." That's what I'd expect.
